Subject: Mutual Action Plan — Unit-Econ Validation & Ops Acceptance (timeline & checkpoints)

Ari —

Following our demo yesterday, attaching a concise MAP itemization for the evaluation + close. Focus here is the unit-econ checks we discussed (tokens/$, caching, batching windows) so procurement and engineering can sign off before the pilot go/no-go. See attached workbook (map_unit-econ_sanity.xlsx) and a small traffic sample (sample_traffic_profile.json).

Summary of assumptions I'm starting from (please flag anything incorrect):
- Per-request breakdown: average prompt = 420 tokens, average generated response = 860 tokens -> ~1,280 tokens per call.
- Expected pilot QPS: 0.25 avg, 2.2 peak (per region).
- Caching: we expect 18% effective prefix reuse on typical query surface (dedupe + session-level caching).
- Batching window: we plan a 12ms batching latency window for latency-sensitive calls and 60ms for background bulk ops.
- Quantization/variant: using q4_0 variant for hosted pilot; fallback to q4_1 for higher-quality prompts increases tokens/$ by ~12%.
- Target unit-econ threshold for acceptance: <= $0.0012 per token-equivalent (defined in workbook).

Proposed gating for MAP acceptance (short):
1) Accuracy gate: baseline QA eval delta <= 3% vs current golden prompts.
2) Unit-econ gate: modeled tokens/$ at pilot traffic must be <= target in three scenarios (median, +30% peak, -20% long-tail).
3) Ops gate: 99th pctl latency under 1.1s for interactive routes with batching window constraints.
4) Security/procurement: SOC2 evidence + contract redlines agreed.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm pilot QPS and any expected burst patterns (Maya on procurement side)?
- Are there any constraints on retaining prompt text in cache for dedupe?
- Please review the workbook and call out any incorrect token-length assumptions.

I'll schedule a 30-min interlock with engineering (Karthik) and procurement (Kimberly) early next week to walk the map and lock timelines. Targeting pilot start: 2028-10-09.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear write-up and attachments. A couple quick clarifying points from our side before we dig into the workbook: 
- Pilot QPS: our product analytics team gives a median of ~0.18 qps per instance and a 95th percentile of ~1.8 qps. Expect spiky behavior around 09:00 UTC and 17:00 UTC.
- Burst behavior: during weekend promotions we see 4–5x spikes but they last < 10m. We can gate those out of the initial pilot if needed.
- Caching: we can cache non-PII prefixes and will ask legal if storing PII-derived prefixes is allowed; likely not.

Two asks: 
1) Can you provide a quick worked example in the workbook that converts tokens/use -> monthly cost per MAU (we want to plug our numbers easily)?
2) We need a short timeline for procurement steps so our finance team can plan credit approvals.

I'll have Maya loop in our security lead if the SOC2 artifacts are sufficient; otherwise expect a short evidence list request.

—Ari

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — Unit-Econ Validation & Ops Acceptance (timeline & checkpoints)

Ari — good questions. I updated the workbook with a short worked example and an ops checklist. Paste of the core worked example here so it's visible in thread: 

Worked example (median scenario):
- Avg tokens/call = 1,280 (prompt + response)
- Effective caching reduction = 18% -> billed tokens/call = 1,049.6
- Calls per user/month = 1,200 (approx; product estimate) -> tokens/user/month = 1,259,520
- Tokens per dollar (platform price after committed discount) = 1,200,000 tokens / $1.00 -> tokens/$ = 1,200,000
- Cost/user/month = tokens/user/month / tokens_per_dollar = 1,259,520 / 1,200,000 = $1.05 per MAU

Sensitivity slices in the workbook (added):
- +30% response size (long-form answers)
- Reduced cache efficacy (10%)
- Batch window tightening for sub-200ms latency routes (less batching efficiency -> +7% cost)

MAP acceptance checklist (detailed):
- Product QA: baseline sims + golden-prompt eval (owner: MedForge product)
- Cost model: finance sign-off on tokens/$ assumptions and committed discount (owner: MedForge finance + Redwood sales)
- Ops: staging load test with 2x peak for 30m; observe batching efficiency and 95/99 pctl latencies (owner: Redwood infra)
- Security: SOC2 + data retention policy and cache TTLs papered (owner: MedForge security + Redwood security)
- Procurement: PO or committed credit by 2028-09-28 to meet pilot start 10-09

Proposed timeline: 
- 2028-09-18: cost model walk (30m) — confirm tokens/$ and discount baseline
- 2028-09-22: staging perf run and caching validation (ops)
- 2028-09-25: procurement finalization and signature window opens
- 2028-10-05: final greenlight checklist review
- 2028-10-09: pilot start

Next steps: I'll send a calendar invite for the cost model walk on 2028-09-18 at 10:00am PT. Karthik will bring the ops testing plan; Kimberly will own procurement timeline and doc list.

Jordan

On the tokens/$ threshold: we set the initial target at $0.0012 per token-equivalent. With the example above, that translates to the $1.05 MAU number. If procurement wants a lower MAU number we can iterate on committed discounts, batching aggressiveness for background routes, and prefetching/caching improvements.

Quick ack from infra side — I've drafted the staging load plan and will attach a short runbook before the 9/22 test. Two small ops notes: 
- For the 12ms batching window, we'll need to increase worker concurrency by ~20% to avoid queuing under the 2x stress. That changes perf-cost tradeoffs; I'll include an ops cost delta in the runbook.
- Prefetch: Redwood can enable session-level prefetching for 30% of traffic patterns identified in the sample profile; this will materially improve the tokens/$ in the median scenario.

I'll upload the runbook to the shared Drive and confirm the invite time.
